description:
Tiramisu Ice Cream in the Ninja Creami – Will It Work? 🤔🍨

Description:
Today, I’m attempting to make Frozen Tiramisu in the Ninja Creami! ☕🍨 Will this creamy, coffee-infused dessert work in a frozen form? I’ll be experimenting with cream cheese, espresso, chocolate, and a rich ice cream base to see if we can capture the classic flavors of tiramisu in a scoopable, ultra-smooth ice cream.

I’ll take you through the process step-by-step, from prepping the mix to spinning it in the Ninja Creami. Will this be a decadent frozen masterpiece or a creamy disaster? Watch to find out!

💬 Have you tried making tiramisu ice cream? Let me know your favorite tips or Ninja Creami hacks in the comments!

📌 Things you'll need:
✔️ Mascarpone/Cream Cheese
✔️ Espresso or Strong Coffee
✔️ Chocolate
✔️ Ladyfinger Cookies


🔔 Subscribe for More Ice Cream Experiments!
If you love frozen treats, food science, and unique ice cream flavors, hit that subscribe button and join me on this delicious journey! 🍦

comments.text:
I use Allulose for artificial sweetener. Sometimes I cut it with Splenda to keep my ice cream from having a paste-like texture. Splenda will increase the freezing point.

Regarding your dairy issue: sounds like you might be lactose intolerant. I am, and it can make one rather miserable. Check the nutrition label on dairy products. If the dairy product has zero sugars and zero added sugars that means there is no lactose in that dairy product. I use Lactaid brand dairy products. They are lactose free.

Good luck.

comments.text:
It appears as if you suffer from both, food and chemical sensitivities.
Lactose intolerance (gas, abdominal disconfort, etc) can be alleviated with digestive enzymes, Walmart has fast acting  'Dairy Digestive' ; however, they do not help if there is caseine sensitivity .
Caseins are metabolized into opioid-like peptides called caso-morphins which attach to opioid receptors in the brain hence, we love cheeses so much .
On the other hand, sugar alcohols (sorbitol, xylitol, mannotol, erythritol, isomalt, lactotol) are not processed by amylase as it happens with table sugar, flours, starches, they are broken  down by the liver which could explain the shaking you experience with one of those.
Some people are highly sensitive to casein A1 therefore they consume milk produced by cows that only produce A2 Beta Casein because they lack the gene for A1. Publix sells the brand a2 Milk , some other people tolerate goat milk, found @ Trader Joe's and Whole Foods
Meyenberg goat milk is high in A2 as well.
Hopefully the info above is somehow helpful to you.
Good luck
